configs.description: Dual 850 W AC supplies, back-to-front airflow - the -B ordering codes. BOTH faces' airflow regions swap: the front becomes the exhaust and the rear the intake. No handle colour is overridden: every rear either document draws is red, and neither shows a -B unit; see the fan-handle-colour-by-airflow gap.
configs.name: ac-b2f

configs.description: Dual 850 W AC supplies, front-to-back airflow - the -F ordering codes.
configs.name: ac-f2b

configs.description: The chassis as it ships: two 850 W AC supplies and four fan trays in, every cage empty. THE AIRFLOW IS WHAT THE ORDERING CODES VARY, so the two orderable builds below carry it - ten OZ codes, five front-to-back and five back-to-front across five power cord regions - and nothing else in the table differs.
configs.name: base

gaps.wanted: THE ONE-BASED AS7816-64X-O SERIES IS NOT MODELLED, and the documents disagree about which numbering they draw. The ordering table sells two base models whose only stated difference is that the O prints ports, fans and supplies from one and the OZ from zero; it also offers the 48 V DC supply only in the O series. The datasheet's elevations are the O, the guide's front enlargement is the OZ, and the guide's rear prints fans 4..1 beside a front that says PSU 0. This device is the OZ and prints fans 3..0 on the datasheet's word. A second device, or a silkscreen that can vary by configuration, would carry the O; a photograph of a real OZ rear settles its fan legend.

WHERE THE LAMPS OF THE TWO INNER PORT ROWS ARE. The vendor states four lamps per port and the outer rows show them, four round lamps above the top row and below the bottom. The inner rows - the upper cages' bottom row and the lower cages' top row - show none in either document: the band between the cages carries only the numeral and arrow legend, and each cage's white belly strip carries six round features per column, which is neither four nor eight and matches the cage's own light-pipe and vent pattern. 32 ports' lamps are therefore not drawn. A close photograph of one column of a real unit would settle it.

WHETHER THE BACK-TO-FRONT BUILD'S FAN HANDLES ARE A DIFFERENT COLOUR. Both airflows are orderable (-F and -B) and every rear either document draws has red handles. Other Edgecore lines colour the reverse build blue, but a sibling family's convention is not evidence for this one, so both configurations draw red.

FRU CODES FOR THE FAN TRAY AND THE 850 W SUPPLY. The ordering table lists chassis SKUs only; the guide's replacement text names no part. Both FRUs are named for the chassis because no code exists to use instead.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in `attrs.environmental` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 6 bays (rear 6); `physical-context` on port group qsfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

arrows-and-lamp-cutouts.note: TWO LINT RULES STAND ON PURPOSE. L61 x 16: each between-cage arrow pair sits 0.93 mm left of its column, which is where the guide's 8.68 px/mm enlargement puts it - the up-arrow 3.0 mm left of centre and the down-arrow 1.15 mm right, hugging a one-digit numeral on the left and a two-digit one on the right. Centring it would be tidier and wrong. L39 x 32: the outer-row lamp part declares four openings, and the toolchain deliberately does not guess whether they are four holes or one slot - the same standing warning the COR580 (24) and COR550 (40) carry. The side-face rails are ESTIMATED: neither document draws a side, and two recessed rails are this shell family's usual sheet-metal return.

cage-frames.note: Each 2x2 ganged cage is drawn inside a bright metal frame, measured at 5x on the datasheet's front for the first block - x 29.3-69.0, y 17.3-42.6 for the upper cage and 47.0-72.3 for the lower - and repeated on the block lattice. The white strip across each frame's middle is the cage's belly between its two ports.

chassis.note: DATASHEET 'Dimensions (WxDxH): 43.84 x 58.0 x 8.77 cm (17.26 x 22.83 x 3.45 in)' and the guide's 'Size (WxDxH) 438.4 x 580 x 87.7 mm' - two documents, one triple. 438.4 is the body; the ears are placed outside it.

figure-choice.note: Gate 1, and the datasheet's two elevations are not equally trustworthy. THE REAR IS SQUARE: panel 999 x 199 px, aspect +0.42% against 438.4/87.7, 2.279 px/mm on x and 2.269 on y. THE FRONT IS NOT AND IS CROPPED FLUSH: its ink fills the whole 1004 x 198 image, +1.44% on aspect. So the front's box was not trusted as the body until something else said so. A SCALE-FREE RATIO SAYS SO. The first-to-last cage-block span, divided by panel width, reads 0.7271 on the datasheet front and 0.7281 on the guide's front - whose own box is square to 0.15% - so the datasheet image IS the full width and x scales at 2.290 px/mm. Its HEIGHT is the part that is short: the guide puts the two cage strips 0.340 and 0.677 of the way down the panel, the datasheet 0.359 and 0.692, the pattern of about 1.5 mm cropped off the datasheet's top edge. So every vertical position is the datasheet's pixel distance at its x scale, anchored so the midline between the two cage strips falls where the guide puts it, at 44.6 mm. ORTHOGRAPHIC: the sixteen column centres fit x = first + pitch*i + gutter*(i//2) to 0.57 px rms, and a quadratic term buys 0.27 px - under 0.9% across the whole row.

front-ends.note: LEFT END, at 5x on the datasheet and checked against the guide's enlargement: the Reset pinhole at (23.1, 42.6) under its legend, and five system lamps in a column at x 23.1 - Loc, Diag, Fan, PSU 0, PSU 1 - at y 51.8, 54.7, 57.6, 60.8 and 63.9, their legends right-aligned 1.7 mm to the left. A honeycomb vent field runs down the edge below them. RIGHT END: the Mgmt RJ-45 stacked over the Console RJ-45 in one bezel at x 391.7 (17.0 x 24.9), legended Mgmt above and Console below; the USB-A standing on end at (414.4, 27.8), 6.1 x 14.0 with its trident beneath; another honeycomb edge vent; and the pull-out product tab at the bottom right, drawn orange in the guide. THE PORT FIELD SITS ON A LIGHTER PLATE: sampled #35373c against the outer panel's #2d2d31, its edges at x 9.4 and 386.9 and y 11.2 and 73.2 on the datasheet's profiles. The upper lamp row is on it; the lower lamp row, the lower numerals and both perforation rows are on the outer panel. The management cluster is off it. THE MGMT JACK IS LAMPED AND THE CONSOLE IS NOT. The datasheet states 'Management Port LED: Green (10M/100M/1G), Flashing: Activity' and nothing for the console, which is also L76's Ethernet-lamped, console-bare convention.

numbering.note: THE DATASHEET SELLS TWO SERIES THAT DIFFER IN WHAT IS PRINTED. Its ordering table's AS7816-64X-OZ base model says 'port, fan and PSU numbering start at zero'; the AS7816-64X-O base model says 'start at one', and Interfaces callouts 7 and 9 give both PSU namings side by side. Issue #330 asks for the zero-based declaration, and the OZ is the base model listed first, so this is the OZ: ports 0-63, PSU 0 and 1, fans 0-3. THE DRAWINGS DO NOT AGREE WITH EACH OTHER. The datasheet's elevations are the O series - ports 1..64, 'PSU 1' and 'PSU 2', fans 4..1. The guide's front enlargement is the OZ - '1 (up) (down) 32', '33', '35', 'PSU 0', 'PSU 1' - which is the silkscreen modelled here. But the guide's own REAR prints fans 4..1, one-based, on the same page set whose front is zero-based. The words beat the drawings: fans are 0..3, printed right to left, and the disagreement is a gap. THE ORDER IS COLUMN-MAJOR WITHIN EACH HALF. The upper cages' top row carries the even ports 0..30 and their bottom row the odd 1..31; the lower cages carry 32..62 over 33..63. The between-cage band prints each column as 'n (up) (down) m' - the upper cage's lower port and the lower cage's upper one - and the outer rows are numbered above and below.

perforation.note: A row of round holes runs along the top and the bottom of the port field (y 8.8 and 82.5, x 28.7-388.8), and a denser perforated patch sits at the very top of the middle of the panel on the guide's front, x 119.6-296.6 - which the datasheet's front cannot show, its top 1.5 mm being cropped. Holes 2.2 mm on a 3.06 mm pitch on the rows, measured at 5x; the patch's pitch does not resolve at 1.36 px/mm and is drawn as fine perforation.

port-leds.note: FOUR ROUND LAMPS PER PORT ON THE OUTER ROWS, measured at 8.68 px/mm on the guide's enlargement - see edgecore/dcs500-lane-leds@1. They sit on the faceplate above the top row (centres at 13.4 mm) and below the bottom row (76.7 mm), centred on their columns, which the datasheet's elevation confirms at its own resolution. THE TWO INNER ROWS' LAMPS ARE NOT LOCATED and are not drawn - see the gap. The band between the cages carries only the 'n (up) (down) m' legend at every magnification either document offers.

port-pitch.note: The registry's ganged-QSFP 19.00 is carried. With the pitch free the fit reads 19.08, rms 0.30 mm, worst column 0.69; pinned to 19.00 the rms is unchanged and the worst column's residual is 0.73 - pinning costs 0.04 mm. The gutter between cages is measured, 7.52, and the row pitch inside a cage 14.62 - 14.19 across the band between the upper and lower cages.

rear.note: MEASURED on the datasheet's rear at 2.279 px/mm. The supplies sit in the LOWER corners, housings x 18.9-69.8 and 367.7-418.6, y 45.8-85.1. The four fan trays fill the middle on a 68.32 mm pitch fitted on the webs between them - see edgecore/dcs500-fan@1 - from x 88.58, y 22.9-85.5. Above each supply a grounding plate carries two screws under a ground symbol, and the upper band carries each tray's numeral. The chassis prints each supply's name above its outer top corner.

sources.note: Two documents, both docling-converted. dcs500-datasheet (the DCS500 / AS7816-64X data sheet) carries the spec list, the nine-callout Interfaces table, the ordering table and on page 2 a colour front and rear elevation, 1004 px wide each. dcs500-qsg (the AS7816-64X quick start guide, six pages) carries small line-art front and rear elevations (600 and 591 px), an enlargement of the front's left end at 8.68 px/mm, a DC terminal-block figure and the hardware specification table. Both letter the artwork AS7816-64X, this device's vendor alias. The guide carries the vendor's standard 'drawings ... are for illustration only' disclaimer, which turns out to matter here - see the numbering note.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 32 QSFP pairs (port-0/port-1 to port-62/port-63). 32 of these were drawn with the upper cage turned before the std cage art moved its lip to the bottom of the opening; turning them keeps the lips in the middle band where they were drawn and seats every optic bail-outward.

weight.note: '14.11 kg (31.1 lb)' in the datasheet, and the guide qualifies the same figure 'with two installed PSUs', so it is the populated machine.
